newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EASDAQ approves rules for September 30 launch.
newsitem.headline: EASDAQ approves rules for September 30 launch.

text.p: The board of EASDAQ, Europe's newest growth stocks market, approved on Friday the exchange's rule book, taking it one step nearer to its planned September 30 launch, officials said.

"The rule book must now go to Belgium's ministry of finance for approval. Once it has been legally accepted the companies we have been talking to can formally apply for a listing," EASDAQ executive Chris Pickles told Reuters.
Because firms can only apply to have their prospectuses cleared once the finance ministry has cleared the rules, EASDAQ was likely to start with fewer listings than hoped for a year ago, he said.

EASDAQ director Jacques Putzeys told Belgian newspaper L'Echo this week he believed listings would start in October and build up gradually to include 10 to 15 companies by year end. In an interview with Reuters last November he had said EASDAQ hoped to start trading with around 25 companies.

But this has not stopped banks and brokerages from around the world from signing up to bankroll the bourse through its start-up phase. The number of EASDAQ shareholders is expected to rise to around 90 from 40 last May even though its business plan does not foresee break even until the fourth year of operations.
"There could be companies there on day one. It depends on the administrative process...but the goal of 50 companies at the end of the first year looks conservative," Pickles said.
EASDAQ hopes to encourage some of the 80 European companies listed on the U.S. NASDAQ exchange, upon which it is modelled, to seek a secondary listing.
Pickles said, however, that many of its shareholders were asking it to focus instead on initial public offerings (IPOs).
Belgian bio-tech firm Innogenetics, which is 12.5 percent owned by Kredietbank NV and Canada's NASDAQ-listed bio-tech firm DynaMotive have already said they will seek EASDAQ listings.
Pickles said a German and a French company were also interested.
EASDAQ will charge companies between 7,500 and 25,000 Ecus for a listing, depending on whether they are seeking an IPO and their market capitalisation.
To qualify they must have total assets of 3.5 million Ecus and capital and reserves of 2 million Ecus.

EASDAQ companies each must be supported by at least two market makers, and market members must be members of the exchange (but not necessarily shareholders). Pickles said around 55 EASDAQ shareholders also qualifed as members.
The others comprised of venture capital companies, law firms or other organisations, such as NASDAQ itself, that will bring companies to the market or provide support services.

Although EASDAQ is based in Brussels, trading will be screen based and carried out anywhere in the European Union. Traders will be linked by a computer system modelled on TRAX, the International Securities Markets Association communications system, and deals will be settled by Switzerland's INTERSETTLE.
"We aim to have about 400 companies in four years time, when we expect to break even," said Jan Van Heuverswyn of Interel, EASDAQ's Belgian public relations firm.
